title: Experimental candidate dcp-jcs-v2, phase 3: signed bundles and the bytes verifier
status: experimental, opt-in; dcp-jcs-v1 stays the default

how_to_read.bases: Whole inputs as ASCII JSON text: signed bundles (keys from fixed seeds), the V1 conformance bundle, and null.
how_to_read.cases[].input: The base, then each edit in order on its bytes: find/replace (find occurs exactly once), find/replace_hex, prefix/suffix, prefix_hex, drop_last. input_sha256 is the hash of the result.
how_to_read.expected.route: The phase 2 route: outcome, and class, detail, offset (relative to the unit) and profile for a rejection, profile_source and the warning classes for v1_path.
how_to_read.expected.adapter_calls: How many times the historical adapter is consulted (phase 2).
how_to_read.expected.entered: The verifier that ran, at most one: none, dcp-jcs-v1 (today's verifier, on the decoded value) or dcp-jcs-v2.
how_to_read.expected.verification: null when no verifier ran; otherwise the verdict and substrings every error list must contain, per SDK.
how_to_read.expected.manifest_sha256 / canonical_sha: For a verified candidate: the hash of the canonical manifest (signature.manifest_hash) and of the canonical unit.
how_to_read.by_adapter: The expectation for one adapter where it differs, keyed "<sdk>:<adapter name>".
how_to_read.now: The instant every verifier that takes one uses. The bases are valid from 2026-10-21 to 2099-12-31; a verifier on the wall clock depends on it falling in that window.
how_to_read.trust: A verified bundle grants no trust or admission and authorizes nothing.

Not walkable: a decoder that drops the BOM reads v1 and the bundle is delegated (TextDecoder, json.loads on bytes); one that keeps it refuses the unit, which is rejected.

A V1 bundle (no manifest, risk_score 0.21): delegated with the diagnosis. Today's V2 verifiers reject it, except the WASM binding, which verifies a V1 bundle when no policy is given; that difference is kept.

An integer literal beyond binary64. JSON.parse and json.loads read Infinity, which is delegated and rejected; serde_json refuses it and Rust has no value to delegate; Go delegates the bytes and its parser refuses them; WASM w1 sends JSON.stringify of Infinity (null), w2 the text, which serde_json refuses.
A decoded null is data: it is delegated, and today's verifier rejects it.
